newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Lack of buying interest pushes Irish bonds lower.
newsitem.headline: Lack of buying interest pushes Irish bonds lower.

text.p: A lack of buying interest pushed Irish bonds lower in late trade on Monday as the market awaited the release of key U.S. economic data later this week, dealers said.
"People are focusing on the key figures due out of the U.S. this week. Ahead of that data, the market is bit drifty. People just don't want to know about buying the market," one dealer said.
"We have seen a bit of underperformance against Germany since Friday and that is purely down to lack of interest," the dealer added.

By 1450 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was down 11 pence from Friday's close at 101.54 to yield 6.08 percent while the key benchmark eight percent bond due 2006 had eased 15 pence from the close to 107.90 to yield 6.81 percent.
Dealer said Irish bonds were yielding 141 basis points over German bunds in the five-year area and 91 basis points over Germany in the 10-year area.

U.S. unemployment, average hourly earnings, lead indicators and real quarterly GDP due out later in the week will be gone through with a fine toothcomb for further clues to interest rate moves in the U.S.
As usual a strong payroll number will rekindle fears of rising interest rates in the world's biggest economy, dealers said.
Dealers said Tuesday's U.S. employment cost index and the UK's final March M4 and lending figures will also be of interest.
